_readme: Single source of truth for final-project dates. Assignments have no due dates.
Dates are stored as (week, day) offsets, not calendar dates, so rolling the
course to a new year means editing the `term` block only -- every deadline
week: 1 = the week containing term.first_class_day. Weeks start on Monday.
day : Mon | Tue | Wed | Thu | Fri.
anchor: 'term' (default) counts weeks from the first class week.
'finals' counts weeks from term.finals_week_starts, so week 1 of the
finals anchor is finals week itself.
Not yet read by syllabus/ or the course calendar, which still compute or
_submission_readme: ONE permanent submission form for the whole course: an Apps Script web app
whose source is assignments/webform/. Everything students upload -- every
assignment and the final project -- is written straight into a Google Drive
folder, organised as <year>/<assignment>/. assignments/submission in this
repository is a symlink to that folder, and .gitignore excludes it.
`url` is the /exec URL of the deployed web app. It does not change year to
year, and it changes only if you create a NEW deployment rather than a new
version of the existing one. Referenced from the assignment sources as
{{submission}}, so it is never typed out twice.
`drive_folder_id` is the Drive id of the destination folder, which is what
the web app is configured with (DEFAULT_FOLDER_ID in
_materials_readme: The Google Drive shared-folder link students use to download everything:
the qmd and its data files, for every assignment.
`publish_dir` is the local path of the Drive folder that holds the year
assignments/students/<year>/ into it. Copying does not share it: run
shareMaterials() in the Apps Script project, which shares THE YEAR FOLDER
only and prints the `url` and `year` lines to paste below.
The build warns while `url` is empty and fails if `year` disagrees with
NEVER share assignments/ or the repo root: that would expose keys/ (the
answer keys) and submission/ (other students' work).
